## The task

Have the model build an NPV/IRR business case for a project you invent, then run the [Editor prompt](../ai.qmd#editor) against it with the instruction to interrogate *who produced the forecast inputs and what their incentives were*.

**Deliverable.** The case, the attack, and your judgement: which criticisms are real and which are the model manufacturing objections because you told it to.

## Tutor prompt for this week

Run this before you read the notes, and again after.

```text
Be my tutor on project selection and business cases. One question at a time,
no lecturing. Make me compute, then make me distrust my own computation —
push me on who produced the forecast inputs and what their incentives were.
```

## The weekly loop

This lab is step 4–6 of the loop. The whole cycle:

```text
1. TUTOR (diagnostic)  — 10 min — what do I already wrongly believe?
2. Read the module     — 20 min — notes + one primary source
3. TUTOR (voice)       — 20 min — one question at a time, no lecturing
4. Write something     — 15 min — a plan, an argument, a worked problem
5. EDITOR              — 10 min — attack what I wrote
6. ROOMMATE            —  5 min — where else does this structure appear?
7. TUTOR (retrieval)   —  5 min — mixed questions from all prior weeks
```

Steps 4 and 5 do the work. A loop that stops after step 3 feels productive and mostly isn't.

## Submission

Upload to Blackboard as a single PDF. Include your prompts. Label every AI-produced element and attach the verification, per the [AI policy](../syllabus.qmd#artificial-intelligence-policy).
